description: A machine costs $24000, has a salvage value of $4000, and a useful life of 5 years. Using straight-line depreciation, what is the annual depreciation expense?
explanation: Straight-line depreciation = (Cost - Salvage Value) / Useful Life = ($24000 - $4000) / 5 = $20000 / 5 = $4000 per year.
hint: (Cost - Salvage) / Life

description: A company has net income of $45000, interest expense of $5000, and income tax expense of $15000. What is EBIT?
explanation: EBIT (Earnings Before Interest and Taxes) = Net Income + Interest Expense + Income Tax Expense = $45000 + $5000 + $15000 = $65000. EBIT measures operating profitability before financing and tax costs.
hint: EBIT = Net Income + Interest + Taxes

description: On March 1, a company receives $18000 cash for a 6-month service contract. What is the journal entry on March 1?
explanation: Receiving cash before performing the service creates a liability (unearned revenue). Debit Cash $18000 (asset increases) and credit Unearned Revenue $18000 (liability increases). Revenue will be recognized as services are performed.
choice3: Debit Accounts Receivable $18000, Credit Service Revenue $18000

description: Using the double-declining-balance method, a $10000 asset with a 5-year life has what depreciation expense in Year 1?
explanation: DDB rate = 2 / Useful Life = 2 / 5 = 40%. Year 1 depreciation = Book Value x DDB Rate = $10000 x 40% = $4000. The DDB rate is twice the straight-line rate and is applied to the remaining book value each year.
hint: DDB Rate = 2 / Life; Depreciation = Book Value x Rate

description: Current assets = $90000, current liabilities = $30000, inventory = $20000, prepaid expenses = $5000. What is the quick ratio?
explanation: Quick Ratio = (Current Assets - Inventory - Prepaid Expenses) / Current Liabilities = ($90000 - $20000 - $5000) / $30000 = $65000 / $30000 = 2.17. The quick ratio excludes less-liquid current assets.
hint: Quick Ratio = (CA - Inventory - Prepaid) / CL

description: A company starts the period with 100 units at $10 each. During the period it buys 200 units at $12 each. It sells 150 units. Using FIFO, what is the cost of goods sold?
explanation: FIFO sells the oldest inventory first. First 100 units sold at $10 = $1000. Next 50 units sold at $12 = $600. Total COGS = $1000 + $600 = $1600. The remaining 150 units in ending inventory cost $12 each = $1800.
hint: FIFO: sell oldest first

description: A company's fiscal year ends December 31. Employees earn $5000 per week (Monday through Friday). The last payroll was paid December 26 (a Friday). December 31 is a Wednesday. What accrual is needed?
explanation: Employees worked 3 days (Mon Dec 29, Tue Dec 30, Wed Dec 31) after the last pay period. Daily wage = $5000 / 5 = $1000/day. Accrual = 3 days x $1000 = $3000. Debit Salaries Expense $3000, Credit Salaries Payable $3000.
hint: Daily wage = weekly / 5; Multiply by days worked

description: Sales = $500000, COGS = $300000, Operating Expenses = $100000, Interest Expense = $20000, Tax Rate = 25%. What is net income?
An asset costs $50000, has a salvage value of $5000, and a useful life of 9 years. Using sum-of-years-digits (SYD), what is the depreciation in Year 1?
explanation: SYD = n(n+1)/2 = 9(10)/2 = 45. Depreciable base = Cost - Salvage = $50000 - $5000 = $45000. Year 1 fraction = 9 / 45. Year 1 depreciation = $45000 x (9 / 45) = $45000 x 0.2 = $9000.
hint: SYD = n(n+1)/2; Year 1 dep = Base x (n/SYD)

description: Beginning inventory = 50 units at $20. Purchases: 100 units at $25. Sales = 80 units. Using the weighted average cost method, what is COGS?
explanation: Weighted average cost = Total Cost / Total Units = (50 x $20 + 100 x $25) / (50 + 100) = ($1000 + $2500) / 150 = $3500 / 150 = $23.33 per unit. COGS = 80 x $23.33 = $1866.67, rounded to $1867.
hint: Avg Cost = Total Cost / Total Units; COGS = Units Sold x Avg Cost

description: A company buys equipment worth $40000 by paying $10000 cash and financing the rest with a 3-year note. What journal entry records this?
explanation: Buying an asset with partial cash and partial note: debit Equipment $40000 (full cost), credit Cash $10000 (asset paid), credit Notes Payable $30000 (liability created for the financed portion).
choice0: Debit Equipment $40000, Credit Cash $10000, Credit Notes Payable $30000
choice2: Debit Cash $10000, Debit Notes Payable $30000, Credit Equipment $40000

description: A company has net income of $80000 and average stockholders equity of $400000. What is the return on equity (ROE)?
explanation: Return on Equity = Net Income / Average Stockholders Equity = $80000 / $400000 = 0.20 or 20%. ROE measures how effectively the company is using shareholders' investment to generate profit.
hint: ROE = Net Income / Average Equity

description: A company prepays $24000 for a 24-month office lease on July 1, Year 1. On December 31, Year 1, what is the adjusting entry?
explanation: By December 31, 6 months of the 24-month lease have expired. Monthly expense = $24000 / 24 = $1000. Expense for 6 months = $1000 x 6 = $6000. Debit Rent Expense $6000, Credit Prepaid Rent $6000.
hint: Monthly exp = Total / Months; Expense = Monthly x Months Used
choice1: Debit Rent Expense $6000, Credit Prepaid Rent $6000
choice2: Debit Rent Expense $24000, Credit Prepaid Rent $24000
choice3: Debit Rent Expense $12000, Credit Prepaid Rent $12000

description: Total assets = $500000. Debt-to-equity ratio = 1.5. What is total equity?
explanation: Debt-to-equity = Liabilities / Equity = 1.5, so Liabilities = 1.5 x Equity. Assets = Liabilities + Equity, so $500000 = 1.5E + E = 2.5E. Equity = $500000 / 2.5 = $200000.
hint: Assets = Liabilities + Equity; D/E = Liabilities / Equity

description: An asset with a book value of $8000 (cost $20000, accumulated depreciation $12000) is sold for $10000. What is the gain or loss?
explanation: Gain/Loss = Sale Price - Book Value = $10000 - $8000 = $2000 gain. Book value = Cost - Accumulated Depreciation = $20000 - $12000 = $8000. Since the sale price exceeds book value there is a gain.
hint: Book Value = Cost - Accum. Dep.; Gain/Loss = Sale Price - Book Value

description: A company has sales of $600000 and average inventory of $100000. What is inventory turnover and the average days to sell inventory?
explanation: Inventory Turnover = COGS / Avg Inventory. Using sales as a proxy: 600000 / 100000 = 6 times. Days in inventory = 365 / 6 = 60.8 days, approximately 61 days.
hint: Inv. Turnover = Sales / Avg Inv; Days = 365 / Turnover

description: A company estimates 2% of credit sales of $200000 will be uncollectible. Record the bad debt entry using the income statement approach.
explanation: Using the percentage of sales (income statement) approach: Bad Debt Expense = 2% x $200000 = $4000. Debit Bad Debt Expense $4000, Credit Allowance for Doubtful Accounts $4000.
choice0: Debit Accounts Receivable $4000, Credit Bad Debt Expense $4000
choice1: Debit Bad Debt Expense $4000, Credit Allowance for Doubtful Accounts $4000
choice2: Debit Allowance for Doubtful Accounts $4000, Credit Bad Debt Expense $4000

description: Net income = $70000. Depreciation = $15000. Accounts receivable increased $8000. Inventory decreased $5000. Accounts payable increased $3000. What is operating cash flow (indirect method)?
explanation: Operating CF = Net Income + Depreciation + Decrease in AR(-)/+ + Decrease in Inv(+) + Increase in AP(+). CF = $70000 + $15000 - $8000 + $5000 + $3000 = $85000.
hint: OCF = NI + Depreciation +/- Changes in Working Capital

description: A company reports: EPS = $4.00 and the stock price is $60. What is the price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio?
explanation: P/E Ratio = Market Price per Share / Earnings per Share = $60 / $4 = 15. A P/E of 15 means investors are paying $15 for every $1 of earnings.
hint: P/E = Market Price / EPS

description: On November 1, a company lends $30000 at 6% annual interest. The fiscal year ends December 31. What interest revenue should be accrued?
explanation: Interest accrued = Principal x Rate x Time = $30000 x 6% x (2 / 12) = $30000 x 0.06 x 0.1667 = $300. Two months (November and December) of interest must be accrued even though cash is not yet received.
hint: Interest = Principal x Rate x (Months / 12)

description: A company using LIFO has a LIFO reserve of $40000. Pretax income under LIFO is $100000. The tax rate is 30%. What would pretax income be under FIFO?
explanation: Under FIFO pretax income = LIFO pretax income + LIFO reserve change. If the LIFO reserve is the cumulative difference, FIFO pretax income = $100000 + $40000 = $140000. FIFO typically results in higher income when prices are rising.
hint: FIFO Income = LIFO Income + LIFO Reserve

description: A company issues 1000 shares of $1 par value common stock at $15 per share. Record the journal entry.
explanation: When stock is issued above par value the excess over par is recorded as Additional Paid-in Capital. Total cash = 1000 x $15 = $15000. Common Stock (par) = 1000 x $1 = $1000. APIC = $15000 - $1000 = $14000.
choice1: Debit Common Stock $1000, Credit Cash $15000, Debit APIC $14000
choice2: Debit Cash $15000, Credit Common Stock $1000, Credit Additional Paid-in Capital $14000

description: A company has total assets of $300000, long-term liabilities of $80000, and current liabilities of $50000. What is the stockholders equity?
explanation: Stockholders Equity = Total Assets - Total Liabilities = $300000 - ($80000 + $50000) = $300000 - $130000 = $170000. This uses the basic accounting equation rearranged.
hint: Equity = Assets - Liabilities

description: A company buys a vehicle for $30000, expects to drive it 150000 miles total, and estimates a salvage value of $3000. In Year 1 the vehicle is driven 30000 miles. What is depreciation under the units-of-production method?
explanation: Units-of-production rate = (Cost - Salvage) / Total Units = ($30000 - $3000) / 150000 = $0.18 per mile. Year 1 depreciation = 30000 miles x $0.18 = $5400.
hint: Dep rate = (Cost - Salvage) / Total units; Dep = Rate x Units used

description: Net income = $120000, interest expense = $10000, tax expense = $30000, total assets = $800000. What is the return on assets (ROA)?
explanation: ROA = Net Income / Average Total Assets = $120000 / $800000 = 0.15 or 15%. Some versions use (Net Income + After-tax Interest) in the numerator, but the basic formula uses net income divided by total assets.
hint: ROA = Net Income / Total Assets

description: Which of the following would be classified as an investing activity on the statement of cash flows?
explanation: Purchasing land is an investing activity because it involves acquiring a long-term asset. Paying dividends is a financing activity. Paying salaries and collecting from customers are operating activities.

description: A company accrues wages of $8000 at December 31 and pays them on January 5 of the next year. Show the January 5 entry.
explanation: At December 31 the company debited Wages Expense and credited Wages Payable for $8000 (the accrual). On January 5 when cash is paid the liability is eliminated: debit Wages Payable $8000, credit Cash $8000.
choice3: Debit Wages Expense $8000, Credit Wages Payable $8000

description: A company has net income of $200000, preferred dividends of $20000, and 90000 weighted average common shares outstanding. What is EPS?
explanation: EPS = (Net Income - Preferred Dividends) / Weighted Average Common Shares = ($200000 - $20000) / 90000 = $180000 / 90000 = $2.00 per share.
hint: EPS = (Net Income - Preferred Dividends) / WACSO

description: On September 1, a company receives $36000 for a 12-month service contract. By December 31 how much revenue has been earned and what remains in unearned revenue?
explanation: By December 31 the company has performed 4 months of service (Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec). Monthly revenue = $36000 / 12 = $3000. Earned revenue = 4 x $3000 = $12000. Unearned balance = $36000 - $12000 = $24000.
hint: Monthly revenue = Total / 12; Earned = Months completed x Monthly

description: At the start of the year retained earnings = $50000. During the year: net income = $30000 and dividends declared = $10000. What is ending retained earnings?
explanation: Ending Retained Earnings = Beginning Retained Earnings + Net Income - Dividends = $50000 + $30000 - $10000 = $70000. This is the standard retained earnings roll-forward formula.
hint: Ending RE = Beginning RE + Net Income - Dividends

description: Year 1: Equipment cost $15000, no salvage value, 5-year life (straight-line). What is book value at the END of Year 2?
explanation: Annual depreciation = $15000 / 5 = $3000. Accumulated depreciation after Year 2 = $3000 x 2 = $6000. Book Value end of Year 2 = $15000 - $6000 = $9000.
hint: Annual dep = Cost / Life; Book Value = Cost - Accum Dep

description: A bond with a face value of $100000 is issued at 98 (98% of face). Record the journal entry.
explanation: Issuing a bond at a discount means cash received is less than face value. Cash = $100000 x 98% = $98000. The $2000 difference is a discount (contra-liability). Debit Cash $98000, Debit Discount on Bonds Payable $2000, Credit Bonds Payable $100000.
choice2: Debit Bonds Payable $100000, Credit Cash $98000, Credit Bond Premium $2000
choice3: Debit Cash $98000, Debit Discount on Bonds Payable $2000, Credit Bonds Payable $100000

description: Beginning accounts receivable = $40000. Ending accounts receivable = $60000. Net credit sales = $500000. What is the average collection period (days)?
explanation: Average AR = ($40000 + $60000) / 2 = $50000. AR Turnover = $500000 / $50000 = 10. Average Collection Period = 365 / 10 = 36.5 days.
hint: Avg AR = (Beg + End) / 2; Turnover = Sales / Avg AR; Days = 365 / Turnover

description: A company sells 500 units at $20 each. Variable cost per unit = $12. Fixed costs = $3000. What is the contribution margin and operating income?
explanation: Contribution margin per unit = Price - Variable Cost = $20 - $12 = $8. Total CM = $8 x 500 = $4000. Operating Income = Total CM - Fixed Costs = $4000 - $3000 = $1000.
hint: CM = (Price - Variable Cost) x Units; OI = CM - Fixed Costs

description: Net income = $50000. Gain on sale of equipment = $8000. Depreciation = $12000. Increase in accounts receivable = $5000. Using the indirect method, what is operating cash flow?
explanation: OCF = Net Income + Depreciation - Gain on Sale - Increase in AR = $50000 + $12000 - $8000 - $5000 = $49000. Gains on asset sales are subtracted (reported in investing), and increases in AR reduce operating cash.
hint: OCF = NI + Dep - Gains + Losses +/- WC changes

description: A company has: Beginning Inventory $10000, Purchases $60000, Ending Inventory $15000. What is Cost of Goods Sold?
explanation: COGS = Beginning Inventory + Purchases - Ending Inventory = $10000 + $60000 - $15000 = $55000. This is the basic COGS formula for a merchandising company.
hint: COGS = Beg. Inv + Purchases - End. Inv

description: When a company changes its inventory costing method from FIFO to weighted average what must it do?
explanation: A change in accounting principle (such as inventory method) requires retrospective application - restating all prior periods as if the new method had always been used. The cumulative effect is recorded as an adjustment to beginning retained earnings.
choice0: Record the change as a current period expense
choice1: Apply the change retrospectively and restate prior period financial statements
choice2: Disclose the change but make no adjustments
choice3: Apply the change only to future inventory purchases

description: A company discovers an error: $5000 of supplies expense was recorded as equipment. Supplies have been fully used. Record the correcting entry.
explanation: The original entry incorrectly debited Equipment and credited Cash. The correct entry should have debited Supplies Expense and credited Cash. To correct: debit Supplies Expense $5000 and credit Equipment $5000 (reverse the wrong debit, record the right debit).

description: A company's quick assets (cash + AR) total $120000 and current liabilities are $80000. What is the quick ratio, and what does it indicate?
explanation: Quick Ratio = Quick Assets / Current Liabilities = $120000 / $80000 = 1.5. A quick ratio above 1.0 indicates the company can cover its current liabilities with its most liquid assets without selling inventory.
hint: Quick Ratio = Quick Assets / Current Liabilities

description: Equipment cost $36000 with no salvage value and a 6-year life. Using double-declining balance, what is the book value at the end of Year 2?
explanation: DDB rate = 2 / 6 = 33.33%. Year 1: $36000 x 33.33% = $12000 depreciation. Book value end Y1 = $24000. Year 2: $24000 x 33.33% = $8000 depreciation. Book value end Y2 = $24000 - $8000 = $16000.
hint: DDB Rate = 2 / Life; Apply rate to book value each year

description: The balance sheet shows: Common Stock $50000, APIC $30000, Retained Earnings $40000, Treasury Stock ($10000). What is total stockholders equity?
explanation: Total Stockholders Equity = Common Stock + APIC + Retained Earnings - Treasury Stock = $50000 + $30000 + $40000 - $10000 = $110000. Treasury stock is subtracted because it is a contra-equity account.

description: A company signs a note payable for $20000 on October 1 at 9% annual interest. The fiscal year ends December 31. What is the interest accrual needed?
explanation: Interest accrued = $20000 x 9% x (3 / 12) = $20000 x 0.09 x 0.25 = $450. Three months of interest (October, November, December) must be accrued. Debit Interest Expense $450, Credit Interest Payable $450.
hint: Interest = Principal x Rate x (Months/12)

description: Given: Sales $400000, Returns $10000, COGS $200000, Selling expenses $50000, Admin expenses $30000, Interest expense $8000, Tax rate 20%. What is net income?
A company sells equipment with a book value of $15000 for $19000 cash. How is this reported on the statement of cash flows?
explanation: The $19000 cash proceeds are reported as a cash inflow in the investing activities section. The $4000 gain ($19000 - $15000) would be subtracted from net income in the operating section (indirect method) since it is already included in the investing section.
choice2: $19000 inflow in operating activities plus $4000 removed
choice3: $19000 inflow in investing activities with $4000 gain removed from operating

description: On April 1, $6000 cash is received for a 1-year service contract. On December 31 (9 months later) what is the adjusting entry?
explanation: Nine months of the 12-month contract have been completed. Earned revenue = 9 / 12 x $6000 = $4500. Debit Unearned Revenue $4500, Credit Service Revenue $4500 to recognize the earned portion.
hint: Earned = (Months completed / Total months) x Total
choice0: Debit Unearned Revenue $6000, Credit Service Revenue $6000
choice1: Debit Unearned Revenue $4500, Credit Service Revenue $4500
choice2: Debit Service Revenue $4500, Credit Unearned Revenue $4500
choice3: Debit Unearned Revenue $1500, Credit Service Revenue $1500

description: Total assets = $1000000. Total liabilities = $600000. Net income = $80000. What is the debt ratio and ROA?
explanation: Debt Ratio = Total Liabilities / Total Assets = $600000 / $1000000 = 0.60 or 60%. ROA = Net Income / Total Assets = $80000 / $1000000 = 0.08 or 8%.
hint: Debt Ratio = Liabilities / Assets; ROA = Net Income / Assets

description: A company purchases a patent for $90000 with a legal life of 20 years and an estimated useful life of 15 years. What is the annual amortization using straight-line?
explanation: Intangible assets are amortized over the shorter of legal life or useful economic life. The useful life is 15 years (shorter than 20). Annual amortization = $90000 / 15 = $6000 per year. Salvage value for intangibles is typically assumed to be zero.
hint: Amortize over the shorter of legal or useful life; Annual = Cost / Life

description: Company uses FIFO. Inventory records: Jan 1 = 200 units at $5. Jan 15 purchase = 300 units at $6. Jan 20 sale = 400 units. What is ending inventory value?
explanation: FIFO sells oldest first. 400 units sold: first 200 at $5 = $1000, next 200 at $6 = $1200, total COGS = $2200. Remaining ending inventory = 100 units at $6 = $600.
hint: FIFO: sell oldest units first; remaining inventory at newest cost

description: Beginning RE = $100000. Net loss for the year = $15000. Cash dividends declared = $5000. Stock dividends declared = $8000. What is ending retained earnings?
explanation: Ending RE = Beginning RE - Net Loss - Cash Dividends - Stock Dividends = $100000 - $15000 - $5000 - $8000 = $72000. Both cash and stock dividends reduce retained earnings.
hint: Ending RE = Beginning RE +/- Net Income(Loss) - Dividends

description: Under IFRS which method of presenting the statement of cash flows uses operating cash flows and is generally preferred?
explanation: IFRS encourages (but does not require) the direct method for presenting operating cash flows - showing actual cash inflows and outflows. The indirect method (starting from net income) is also acceptable but the direct method is considered more informative.

description: A company declares a $20000 cash dividend. Record the declaration entry and then the payment entry.
explanation: Declaration: Debit Retained Earnings $20000, Credit Dividends Payable $20000 (creates a liability). Payment: Debit Dividends Payable $20000, Credit Cash $20000 (eliminates the liability). Note: some companies use a Dividends Declared account instead of debiting RE directly.
choice0: Declaration: Debit RE $20000, Credit Div Payable $20000; Payment: Debit Div Payable $20000, Credit Cash $20000
choice1: Declaration: Debit Div Expense $20000, Credit Cash $20000; Payment: No additional entry
choice2: Declaration: Debit Cash $20000, Credit RE $20000; Payment: Debit Div Payable $20000, Credit RE $20000
choice3: Declaration: No entry needed; Payment: Debit RE $20000, Credit Cash $20000

description: Under the indirect method which of the following changes in working capital accounts REDUCES operating cash flow?
explanation: An increase in accounts receivable reduces operating cash flow because cash has not yet been collected even though revenue was recognized. Increases in payables and decreases in receivables or inventory are sources of cash.
